title: Check: probes
description: Five questions on liveness, readiness and startup probes.

questions.prompt: What does a failing liveness probe do?

options.text: Removes the Pod from Service endpoints

questions.explanation: Liveness answers 'is this process wedged?' and the cure is a restart. Removal from endpoints is readiness.

questions.prompt: What does a failing readiness probe do?

options.text: Takes the Pod out of Service endpoints until it passes

questions.explanation: Readiness gates traffic, not lifecycle. A Pod can be alive but not ready - warming a cache, for instance.

questions.prompt: What problem does a startup probe solve?

options.text: A slow-starting app being killed by its own liveness probe

questions.explanation: While the startup probe is running, liveness and readiness are held off - so you can be generous at boot and strict afterwards.

questions.prompt: A container is in CrashLoopBackOff shortly after start, with an aggressive liveness probe. What is the likely fix?

options.text: Raise initialDelaySeconds or add a startup probe

questions.explanation: The probe is killing the app before it has finished starting. Give it room, or gate it behind a startup probe.

questions.prompt: Which probe handler types does Kubernetes support? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: httpGet, exec, tcpSocket and grpc. There is no DNS probe type.
